title: 23rd Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The 23rd sitting opened at 09:01 on Monday 24 November 2025 with 38 members present. The President's nominations of two non-resident ambassadors and five Tax Appeal Tribunal members were sent to committees, and debate on the bill to repeal the Freedom of Peaceful Assembly Act was closed with a vote set for the day's vote hour. MPs then began debating the budget committee's report on the 2026 state budget (MVR 64.2 billion), with government-aligned members mostly backing it and several opposition and independent members criticising the deficit, debt and stalled island projects. The sitting recessed from 10:31 to 13:17 and the budget debate was still running at the end of this part. The text is readable but some marks are dropped, so a few vote intentions are uncertain. The sitting continued the debate on the committee report on the 2026 state budget. Several members spoke about debt repayment, the deficit, hospitals, housing and sewerage projects, with some members arguing the budget figures do not match what was promised and others saying it prioritises health and housing. The chair then held a vote on whether to accept a bill to repeal the 2013 Peaceful Assembly law, which was not accepted, and said the budget debate would resume at the next sitting. The text of the first two speeches in this part (continued from the previous part) has no speaker header here, so those speakers are not listed.

items.title: Matters for a vote: bill to repeal Law No. 1/2013 (Freedom of Peaceful Assembly Act), submitted by the member for South Galolhu

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Opposed repealing the assembly law, saying peaceful protest rights already exist but should not block roads, schools or business.
Supported the 2026 budget, citing about MVR 8.3 billion for development projects and debt repayment, and defended the government's record against past administrations.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: As sponsor, urged repeal of the assembly law and said parties should find common ground, citing the President's earlier pledge on the matter.
Criticised the 2026 budget as favouring defence over health and said unfinished flagship projects, such as the monorail and undersea tunnel, show the problem.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: On the repeal bill, said each side acts in its own interest depending on who governs, and urged less point-scoring.
Presented the budget committee report: totals unchanged apart from MVR 3.5 million restored to the Majlis budget; revenue about MVR 40.4 billion against MVR 64.2 billion spending.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked how much debt was actually repaid last year compared with the figures quoted, and said the budget text should be treated as an agreement with citizens.
Said promised direct subsidies and cash support are not clearly itemised, and questioned large allocations to defence and culture compared with health.
Raised unfinished or underfunded local projects, including the Kulhudhuffushi regional hospital budget and a completed but unopened sewerage system in Vaikaradhoo.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the budget and asked for the Hinmafushi health centre to be upgraded to hospital standard, plus development of Huraa's mangrove and Gulhi.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said he would vote for the budget as last year, but listed stalled Velidhoo projects (harbour, hospital, power, sports ground) and raised concern about debt and housing.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Backed the budget, saying it funds many island offices, health centres, harbours and reclamation, and argued earlier governments left problems unsolved.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Criticised the MVR 64 billion budget for its large deficit and debt, questioned where a MVR 2.7 billion Bank of Maldives agreement money would go, and urged spending cuts.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: As a committee member, supported the budget, urged matching spending to income and recovering lost state funds, and rejected the Hanimaadhoo member's claims.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Said he would vote for the budget in hope of presidential pledges to Addu being met, while criticising rising debt, bank risk and lack of spending cuts.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said committee talks produced little response to opposition requests such as fisheries and agriculture support, and noted a cut to fisheries subsidies.
Raised stalled Hithadhoo projects: Islamic centre, court complex, immigration office and roads.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Said the budget lacks detail on results and that growing public-sector hiring and recurring costs make people dependent on state jobs.
Raised sewerage and water problems in Hithadhoo and Kunahandhoo (Laamu) and school and hospital shortcomings.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Said the budget lacks transparency and project detail, raised Maradhoo health centre, school hall and sports ground needs, and said he could not vote without the detail.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Noted the budget was unchanged by committee with a deficit of about MVR 26 billion, and said projects for Kendhoo, Dhonfanu, Kihaadhoo, Kudarikilu and Kamadhoo have not moved.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Fully supported the committee report, citing allocations for rehabilitation, health buildings, culture, fisheries and the student loan scheme.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the committee report and said the MDP would oppose any budget regardless of quality; his speech was cut off at the end of this part.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Raised a point of order saying remarks about him on debt repayment were inaccurate and that the budget lists specific repayment amounts.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Said the 2026 debt-repayment-adjusted budget is smaller than 2025's and the deficit is falling, and that a budget is changeable, not fixed.
Highlighted health spending, signed housing units and planned Malé housing, and said he supports the committee report.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Said voters gave the President and his party a large majority to deliver quickly, and that the budget puts health first including for Addu City.
Said anti-corruption and governance reform are under way and that he fully supports the budget.

decisions: Two non-resident ambassador nominations (Jordan and Palestine) were sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The five Tax Appeal Tribunal member nominations were sent to the Judiciary Committee.
Debate on the bill to repeal the Freedom of Peaceful Assembly Act was closed, with the bill to be voted on in the day's vote hour.
No amendments were received to the Budget Review Committee report, so the 2026 budget debate proceeded at 7 minutes per member.
The sitting recessed from 10:31 to 13:17 and the chair planned to continue the budget debate until the 14:00 vote hour.
The bill to repeal Law No. 1/2013 (Freedom of Peaceful Assembly) was not accepted by the House.
The chair said the budget debate will continue at the next sitting.
Next sitting set for Tuesday 25 November 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accepting the bill to repeal Law No. 1/2013 (Freedom of Peaceful Assembly); 93 members in total, 60 present, 59 voted, 30 needed
